## Audit report: pi-goal-list-loop-audit — whole-file secret-tag trailing-newline fix

**Objective (parsed):** Fix MEDIUM finding where whole-file secret-tag detection used a single `strip_suffix(b"\n")`, so whole-file-encrypted BINARY secrets with CRLF or 2+ trailing newlines were misrouted (UTF-8-lossy smudge → U+FFFD corruption; or missed double-encrypt guard on clean). Both sites (clean-side guard and smudge-side decrypt) must tolerate arbitrary trailing `\r`/`\n`.

**Findings — evidence-first:**

1. **Commit + identity (contract item 1):** `de343f7` exists on `main`, authored `DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>`, which matches the repo's configured `user.name`/`user.email`. Working tree clean.
2. **Findings box (contract item 2):** `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` line 6 is `- [x] ... — fixed in de343f7`; short hash matches the commit.
3. **Fix is real, not cosmetic:** diff adds `trim_trailing_line_endings` (while-loop stripping all trailing `\r`/`\n`) and replaces both `strip_suffix(b"\n")` call sites — `starts_with_any_secret_tag` (line 283, used by `src/security/src/modules/filter.rs:269` and `:314` full-encrypt/binary branches) and `decrypt_whole_file_tag` (line 870, smudge-side byte-safe path). No live `strip_suffix(b"\n")` sites remain (only doc-comment mentions).
4. **Behavior proven, not just claimed:** the regression test `test_whole_file_tag_tolerates_crlf_and_multiple_newlines` passes — it exercises `\r\n`, `\n\n`, `\r\n\r\n`, `\n\n\n` variants across four surfaces: unit decrypt (byte-identical binary round-trip), production `smudge_with_security` entry, clean-side guard recognition, and end-to-end `smart_clean_with_path(".env")` pass-through (no double encryption). The old single-strip behavior would leave `...]\r` or `...]\n` after stripping, failing the `ends_with(b"]")` check — the mutation claim is consistent with the code by inspection.
5. **Workspace gates independently re-run:** `cargo test --workspace --locked` → 24 suites, 0 failed (incl. dracon-sync 932 passed, dracon-warden integration 10 passed). `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` → clean. (A `failed to push some refs` line in output is an intentional in-test push-failure simulation in dracon-sync, not a failure.)

**Weak/missing evidence:** None material. The only noise is a pre-existing unused-import warning in dracon-sync's test profile, unrelated to this fix and not part of any claimed gate.
